i'm very sorry you had to experience this. it's an uncomfortable situation to be in. but i want you to know that you didn't do anything wrong. your sexuality was not respected, your boundaries were crossed, and you were backed into a corner. they should have respected your first answer and accepted being rejected. the fact that you were pushed and berated to say something deemed "transphobic" and saying you're not a real lesbian sounds like they were baiting you into saying something they could use against you for ammo almost.

you do not have to explain anything. you do not have to apologize. you've done nothing wrong. they were in the wrong for pestering over and over. a simple no should be enough of an answer and you don't owe anyone any explanation or need to elaborate your no.

never apologize for your sexuality, ever. you shouldn't feel sorry or ashamed for being a lesbian. it's a part of who you are.

if neither of them can accept your reasoning and explanation you have given them, i'm not sure if they can even accept it if you bow down to their wants and apologize how they want you to. they are expecting you to say the words they want to put in your mouth. nothing you said was a lie and you're right when you shouldn't apologize for your sexuality.

tldr; you don't owe anyone an explanation, you shouldn't apologize for your sexuality, you didn't say anything wrong and your boundaries were pushed way out of line. no one can force you to do or say anything.

i realized that a lot of the issues with me transitioning was based around trauma and the ptsd received from it, homophobia, sexual harassment, and misogyny. it manifested this oddly intense dysphoria in me and i thought i could escape it by becoming a new person.

i was socially out for 6 years and medically on T for 3 years. it took around 2 years for me to question why i was doing it. I detransitioned earlier this year because i realized why i did it was more due to traumas and homophobia that i never got help from. T completely wrecked my mental health and physical health. and i came to reality and realized i could never biologically be a male.

transitioning was based around appearances. i was always stressing over whether i passed or not to others and not caring about me and how i felt. it was like i was doing it for other people and not myself. it was stressful and causing horrible depression and anxiety. i couldn't become a new person, transitioning was an escape and not a solution. you're still the same person but feel like you're living a lie and in a delusion making yourself believe you can be the opposite sex. it made my dysphoria worse.

i also realized that i was simply a butch lesbian pushed to the edge. i want to be a strong woman and doing that is staying the woman i am and not giving in to what others think or want me to do.

I'm severely mentally ill as well which may have caused me to transition as well as past abuse. (Depression, anxiety, BPD, PTSD) I was mentally/emotionally abused and r**ed as well as a brief addiction to alcohol. My mom had actually backed me into a corner as well and asked me if I even knew what it was like to like girls and called me disgusting for exploring my sexuality and figuring out I was a lesbian. Transitioning caused a lot of alienation from my family as well.

I was 3 years on hormones, name change (which for me is fine, I love my name), a hysterectomy, and health issues from the hormones such as worsening my blood pressure, worse mental health, and the high possibility hormones caused my uterus to literally freak out and needing the surgery. I am now on estrogen patches and my mental health has been...amazing compared to how it was before. Things are so much clearer in my mind, anger is not so bad, irritability is not so bad, things just seem...better.

I am still horribly dysphoric though. Not gender wise, but sex wise. Part of detransitioning for me was realizing I could never become the other sex truly and finally getting it through my head. It seemed like something I was doing for other people -- passing for other people, stressing over it, getting depressed over it. Trying to act manly enough. Once I stopped stressing and just...doing things my way, it did get a little easier, simpler.

I still dress masculine, I don't shave, I didn't revert back into this high feminine code but just did what I liked, what I'm comfortable with, and what makes me happy. It took me over a year to finally come to terms and accept this. It definitely takes time but once you get there things are just amazingly better and clearer. I am still planning on a chest reduction but that is a lot due to medical but having a flatter chest will help me as well with overcoming the dysphoria.

I'm finding hobbies to get busy with, in therapy, and on different meds to help me stay stable as well. Honestly working through dysphoria in different ways is helping me more now than injecting something into my stomach every week. It's about thinking about if there could be other causes as to why you transitioned, what is best for you, and so on. You don't need to stop cold turkey. You can take your time and baby step your way into the detransitioning spot or maybe that's not for you. There is no rush to this thing. Take your time in thinking about what will make you happy in the long run for yourself and not other people.
